coverage_gaps.protocol: RequestArena / RequestSlot explicit-I/O request lifecycle — the load-bearing accepted-request protocol since Phase B.
scope_a_model_would_encode: five-stage admission (reserve -> prepare -> commit -> enqueue -> dispatch)
Scheme-B enqueue/cancel arbitration (cancel-wins vs enqueue-wins, exactly one terminal)
generation increment before slot reuse; stale-key rejection
ready-ring FIFO preserving backend-known terminal order
borrow-through-reap (fd/buffer borrow ends at completion-ready publication)
coverage_gaps.why_no_model_yet: The smallest meaningful isolated protocol has not been modeled. Per AGENTS.md §17 ('Do not invent a model merely for ceremonial coverage. Model the smallest protocol that captures the load-bearing race.'), this gap is accepted as formal debt rather than a blocker. The protocol's correctness is currently established by the executable evidence below, not by a TLA+ abstraction.
current_executable_evidence: request_lifecycle_scheme_b_test (Scheme-B enqueue/cancel arbitration, terminal winner, generation/reuse)
per-backend C2 integration tests (C2b/C2c/C2d/C2e rows on Fake + ThreadPool)
8-13 single-point production mutation executions per C2 class
death tests (fail-fast rollback, stale handle, live pin, open registration)
coverage_gaps.not_covered_by_existing_suites: No suite in this manifest binds request_arena.hpp/request_slot.hpp. The adjacent e7-publication/e8-ownership-transfer suites model Completion claim/publish CAS and ownership transfer (a different protocol — the publication object, not the slot lifecycle); e9-park-wake/e10-waitnode model Scheduler wake/wait-queue primitives; e16-application-runtime models the runtime epoch. None of these models the arena slot state machine, Scheme-B arbitration, generation/reuse, ready-ring, or reap-only publication. Do not read these adjacent suites as RequestArena coverage.
revisit_triggers: before materially changing RequestArena / RequestSlot lifecycle authority
before introducing a second waiter or multi-wait abstraction into the arena
before splitting the terminal-winner or reap-only-publication authority across a second domain
when a future concurrency defect demonstrates that the existing executable evidence does not distinguish the faulty protocol
